beats.text: Both of these pages say booked. Only one booking was saved right. An AI agent said fixed, both times. AccessFinish checks that the user can actually finish.
Here is a real bug in the open-source Easy Appointments app. A keyboard user can't reach the date picker at all.

AccessFinish drives the journey in a real browser, then hands the evidence and the source code to NVIDIA Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory. No root cause is given. Nemotron searches the code, and writes a fix.
beats.say: AccessFinish drives the journey in a real browser, then hands the evidence and the source code to NVIDIA Nemo-tron, on Nebius Token Factory. No root cause is given. Nemo-tron searches the code, and writes a fix.

beats.text: Nemotron makes the date reachable, and the page says the booking is confirmed. But AccessFinish reads the database. Saved for the wrong day. Rejected.
beats.say: Nemo-tron makes the date reachable, and the page says the booking is confirmed. But AccessFinish reads the database. Saved for the wrong day. Rejected.

beats.text: And it shows which code did it. Half a second after the date is typed, the month-change handler fetches unavailable dates, and overwrites what the user typed.
With that evidence, Nemotron fixes the reset, and the right date is saved. But reopening the booking shows today's date. A second bug.
beats.say: With that evidence, Nemo-tron fixes the reset, and the right date is saved. But reopening the booking shows today's date. A second bug.

beats.text: Nemotron fixes that too, building on its best attempt. Verified: saved, reopened in a fresh browser, and the mouse path still works.
beats.say: Nemo-tron fixes that too, building on its best attempt. Verified: saved, reopened in a fresh browser, and the mouse path still works.

beats.text: Across twenty-seven keyboard runs, seventy-seven false booked confirmations were caught. Not one got through.
As a control, we also planted a simple fault: a wrong phone number behind a success page. Nemotron fixed it in all twenty-seven runs, for about a cent each.
beats.say: As a control, we also planted a simple fault: a wrong phone number behind a success page. Nemo-tron fixed it in all twenty-seven runs, for about a cent each.

beats.text: Fifty-four live runs, for under seven dollars of Nemotron. On the real bug, the final agents found a verified fix in two of ten runs. Fixes that are proven, not promised.
